analysis: Examined three changes. (1) EngineV2Factory+DemandedCheckpoint.swift lines 61-78 adds demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens. It is gated on a paged backend, dense Qwen35 (isDenseQwen35), an SSDHybridCheckpointStore, and the paged or native-quantized-paged layout. It returns store.config.minEffectiveTokens, the same floor as the existing dense-Qwen short-checkpoint path (lines 25-27). It is not tied to constructionPurpose, but the existing serving policy already qualifies dense Qwen with the same floor, so this introduces no new qualification bypass. It does add checkpoint ranges that end just below the prompt end. This changes which prefix checkpoints the SSD cache persists (T-041). The at-rest design is unchanged: HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping, DBK3 AES-GCM, 30-minute TTL, and disk budget. Per-donation adoption and benefit gating live in SSDPrefixCache.donate, which is not in this diff. The change plausibly increases donation frequency and SSD write volume for Qwen conversations. Whether the existing endurance, disk and staging guards cap this is not visible here. (2) EngineV2Factory+Production.swift lines 310-311 wires the new policy into schedulerConfig. The inputs match the neighbouring demanded-checkpoint settings. The setting is applied only after the SDK scheduler config is built, and the SDK semantics for demandedLatestCheckpointMinimumTokens are outside the supplied evidence. (3) InferenceErrorClassifier.swift line 42 adds .responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens to the retryable toolNoncompliance reason. This is a typed, content-free classification that emits only the closed enum, so there is no new data exposure. Provider-fault attribution is a semantic choice, not a security regression. Remaining unverified items: the SDK implementation of the latest-checkpoint partition, whether SSD wear and endurance guards bound the extra donations, and that MLXOpenAIServiceError.responseFormatCutOffByMaxTokens exists in the dependency. No concrete security regression is established.
